title: Work Portfolio
text:
This portfolio collects a series of real projects I have developed at work, with a focus on financial data, treasury workflows, and analytics. The projects are designed to be reproducible and demonstrate my skills in data engineering, analysis, and visualization.
This portfolio is a work in progress, and I will continue to add new projects as they are completed. The projects are organized into sections based on their focus area, and each project includes a brief description and a link to the full report.

title: Daily FX Rates — Project Report
text:
Overview
This report documents the maintained FX rates loader in src/daily_fx_rates.py, which fetches daily FX rates from the Frankfurter API and stores them in a CSV file and Neon PostgreSQL table.
The loader normalizes keys before deduplication, backfills missing business-day rows, and tracks provisional rows with fx_quality_flag so they can be revalidated on later runs.


Setup
pip install -r daily-fx-rates/requirements.txt


Run
Run the maintained loader from the repository root:
python src/daily_fx_rates.py
If you want to render the report itself with Quarto:
quarto render daily-fx-rates/report.qmd


Outputs

daily-fx-rates/data/fx_rates.csv
Neon PostgreSQL (table: fx_rates)



Example

        'currency':['USD','EUR','GBP'],
        'fx_to_usd':[1.0,0.91,0.78]

    display(sample)

title: Create Date Table — Project Report
text:
Overview
This mini-project creates and maintains a date_table in PostgreSQL, providing a canonical calendar dimension for reporting.


Setup
Ensure DATABASE_URL is available in the repository .env file.
pip install -r create-date-table/requirements.txt


Run
From the repository root:
python create-date-table/create_date_table.py


Table schema
The script generates a table with calendar_date, year, month, quarter, weekday, is_weekend, is_month_start, is_month_end, and ISO week/year.


Notes
The script is idempotent and inserts only missing dates, making it safe for scheduled incremental runs in CI.


Example: preview calendar rows (safe local sample if DB not available)

import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
from IPython.display import display
csv_path = Path('create-date-table/sample_dates_preview.csv')

else:
    # Generate a small in-memory sample

    dates = pd.date_range(start='2026-07-25', periods=7, freq='D')
    df = pd.DataFrame({'calendar_date': dates.date})
    df['year'] = df['calendar_date'].apply(lambda d: d.year)
    df['month'] = df['calendar_date'].apply(lambda d: d.month)
    df['is_weekend'] = df['calendar_date'].apply(lambda d: d.weekday()>=5)

title: FX Prime Brokerage Collateral
text:
This report documents the FX Prime Brokerage Collateral project as a reproducible analysis. It shows the Python pipeline line by line, renders outputs from the generated CSV files, and connects those calculations to the checked-in Power BI semantic model and dashboard.
The project is synthetic and intended for portfolio demonstration and training. It is not a production margin or collateral engine.


We start by importing the required modules and loading the generated CSV files. The find_project_root() function locates the project folder based on the presence of data/ and src/ subfolders. The four datasets are read into a dictionary of DataFrames for later use.

title: FX Prime Brokerage Collateral
text:
Stage 2: derive limits
generate_limits.py creates a limit schedule for each bank and subtracts the portfolio exposure from the limit:
limit_available_usd = credit_limit_usd - counterparty_exposure_usd
This is a control dataset, not a market valuation. It answers: how much unused counterparty capacity remains? IF the portfolio exposure exceeds the limit, the available capacity will be negative and we should not be able to assign new trades to that bank. Usually, when limits are exceeded, we won’t be able to see the bank offering us any transaction in the market until the limits are back within the threshold.

title: FX Prime Brokerage Collateral
text:
The calculation
The core logic lives in src/generate_mtm_report.py. For each business date:

Initial margin is the minimum amount of cash or collateral deposited with a broker to support a leveraged position. For simplicity, it is calculated as 5% of active trade exposure and is stored as a negative amount because it is owed to the broker.
Variation margin is the aggregated mark-to-market P&L. It keeps its market sign: positive means favourable revaluation and negative means adverse revaluation.
Collateral required is the sum of initial margin and variation margin.
Posted collateral is the amount already posted by the client to the broker.
Excess/deficit compares posted collateral with the positive internal obligation. Negative means more collateral is needed; positive means excess collateral is held.
A deficit schedules a next-day posting to reach the exposure plus a buffer (which is normally around $ 500K).
A surplus above the buffer can trigger a collateral recall.

# Simplified calculation from generate_mtm_report.py
im_raw = 0.05 * exposure
vm_raw = daily_pnl
initial_margin = -im_raw
variation_margin = vm_raw
collateral_required = initial_margin + variation_margin
excess_deficit = collateral_required - collateral_posted   
The current constants are INITIAL_COLLATERAL = 1_000_000, BUFFER = 500_000, MOVE_INCREMENT = 10_000, and MIN_MOVE = 50_000.

title: FX Prime Brokerage Collateral
text:
Visualisation: collateral KPI cards
The Power BI dashboard summarises the latest position with KPI cards. We can create the same type of visual in Python by calculating each metric for the latest reporting date and comparing it with the previous available date.
The values retain the data-model sign convention. For example, Initial Margin and Collateral Required remain negative, while the card change shows the ordinary numerical difference from the previous date.

from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch


def format_amount(value):
    """Format a USD value compactly for a KPI card."""
    absolute_value = abs(value)
    if absolute_value >= 1_000_000:
        return f"{'-' if value < 0 else ''}{absolute_value / 1_000_000:.2f}M"
    if absolute_value >= 1_000:
        return f"{'-' if value < 0 else ''}{absolute_value / 1_000:.0f}K"
    return f"{value:,.0f}"


def format_change(value):
    """Format a numerical daily change with an ASCII direction marker."""
    if value > 0:
        return f"+ {format_amount(value)}"
    if value < 0:
        return f"- {format_amount(abs(value))}"
    return "- 0"


latest_date = mtm_report["report_date"].max()
report_dates = sorted(mtm_report["report_date"].unique())
previous_date = report_dates[-2] if len(report_dates) > 1 else latest_date
latest_report = mtm_report.loc[mtm_report["report_date"] == latest_date].iloc[0]
previous_report = mtm_report.loc[mtm_report["report_date"] == previous_date].iloc[0]

latest_portfolio = portfolio.loc[portfolio["report_date"] == latest_date]
previous_portfolio = portfolio.loc[portfolio["report_date"] == previous_date]

cards = [
    ("Initial Margin", latest_report["initial_margin"], latest_report["initial_margin"] - previous_report["initial_margin"]),
    ("Variation Margin", latest_report["variation_margin"], latest_report["variation_margin"] - previous_report["variation_margin"]),
    ("Collateral Required", latest_report["collateral_required"], latest_report["collateral_required"] - previous_report["collateral_required"]),
    ("Collateral Posted", latest_report["collateral_posted"], latest_report["collateral_posted"] - previous_report["collateral_posted"]),
    ("Excess / Deficit", latest_report["excess_deficit"], latest_report["excess_deficit"] - previous_report["excess_deficit"]),
    ("Total Portfolio (USD)", latest_portfolio["trade_size_usd"].sum(), latest_portfolio["trade_size_usd"].sum() - previous_portfolio["trade_size_usd"].sum()),
    ("Open Positions", latest_portfolio["trade_id"].nunique(), latest_portfolio["trade_id"].nunique() - previous_portfolio["trade_id"].nunique()),
]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(cards), figsize=(19, 2.2))
fig.patch.set_facecolor("#f1f2ed")

for ax, (title, value, change) in zip(axes, cards):
    ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
    ax.axis("off")
    ax.add_patch(
        FancyBboxPatch(
            (0.01, 0.03),
            0.98,
            0.94,
            boxstyle="round,pad=0.015,rounding_size=0.04",
            linewidth=0.8,
            edgecolor="#d9ddd5",
            facecolor="#ffffff",
        )
    )
    value_color = "#1f7a4d" if value >= 0 else "#8b1e2d"
    change_color = "#1f7a4d" if change >= 0 else "#8b1e2d"
    ax.text(0.08, 0.79, title, fontsize=10, color="#6b6f6b", va="center")
    ax.text(0.08, 0.52, format_amount(value), fontsize=17, fontweight="bold", color=value_color, va="center")
    ax.text(0.08, 0.20, f"Change: {format_change(change)}", fontsize=9, color=change_color, va="center")

fig.suptitle(
    f"Collateral snapshot | {latest_date.date()}",
    x=0.01,
    y=1.08,
    ha="left",
    fontsize=12,
    fontweight="bold",
    color="#333333",
)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

title: FX Prime Brokerage Collateral
text:
Project structure
The checked-in PBIP project is under fx-prime-brokerage-collateral/dashboard/:
dashboard/
├── fx-prime-brokerage-collateral.pbip
├── fx-prime-brokerage-collateral.Report/
│   └── definition/pages/
└── fx-prime-brokerage-collateral.SemanticModel/
    └── definition/
        ├── tables/
        ├── relationships.tmdl
        └── model.tmdl
The model contains three principal facts (fx_portfolio, limits, mtm_report), supporting dimensions (dim_date, dim_banks, dim_currencies), an FX rates table, and Measures_Table for reusable DAX.

title: FX Prime Brokerage Collateral
text:
Relationship and filter design
The date dimension filters mtm_report.report_date, fx_portfolio.report_date, and limits.as_of_date. Bank and currency dimensions provide reusable slicer paths. The collateral page should therefore use dim_date[calendar_date] for time controls rather than placing the fact date directly in every visual.
The primary modelling caveat is grain: mtm_report is daily, while fx_portfolio is trade-leg level. Measures must be used when combining these tables so that a visual does not accidentally sum a daily collateral value once per trade.

title: FX Prime Brokerage Collateral
text:
Core DAX measures
These are the central measures already present in Measures_Table.tmdl:
Initial Margin = SUM(mtm_report[initial_margin])
Variation Margin = SUM(mtm_report[variation_margin])
Collateral Required = SUM(mtm_report[collateral_required])
Collateral Posted = SUM(mtm_report[collateral_posted])
Excess / Deficit = SUM(mtm_report[excess_deficit])
Because initial margin and collateral required are stored as negative amounts owed to the broker, inverse measures can be useful for visuals where positive means amount required. Variation margin is different: it must keep its market sign, so it is used directly.
Initial Margin (Inverse) = -1 * SUM(mtm_report[initial_margin])

Variation Margin (Inverse) = SUM(mtm_report[variation_margin])

Collateral Required (Inverse) = -1 * SUM(mtm_report[collateral_required])

title: FX Prime Brokerage Collateral
text:
Previous-day and moving-average patterns
The previous-day pattern finds the latest fact date before the current date selected in the date dimension, then evaluates the measure at that date:
Collateral Posted (Previous Day) =
VAR CurrentDate = MAX(dim_date[calendar_date])
VAR PreviousDateWithData =
    CALCULATE(
        MAX(mtm_report[report_date]),
        REMOVEFILTERS(dim_date),
        dim_date[calendar_date] < CurrentDate
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        [Collateral Posted],
        REMOVEFILTERS(dim_date),
        dim_date[calendar_date] = PreviousDateWithData
    )

Collateral Posted (Daily Change) =
    [Collateral Posted] - [Collateral Posted (Previous Day)]
For smoothing, the existing model uses a 30-day window:
IM 30 Day Moving Average =
CALCULATE(
    AVERAGEX(
        DATESINPERIOD(
            dim_date[calendar_date],
            MAX(dim_date[calendar_date]),
            -30,
            DAY
        ),
        [Initial Margin (Inverse)]
    )
)

title: Treasury Cashflow Simulation — Project Report
text:
Overview
This Quarto report documents the treasury-cashflow-simulation pipeline: how synthetic daily transactions are generated, internal sweeps applied, CSV outputs produced, and results persisted into PostgreSQL.


Setup
Install Treasury Cashflow dependencies from the repository root:
pip install -r treasury-cashflow-simulation/requirements.txt


Run
From the repository root:
python treasury-cashflow-simulation/run_pipeline.py


Pipeline architecture

Entry point: treasury-cashflow-simulation/run_pipeline.py
Main pipeline: treasury-cashflow-simulation/src/simulate_pipeline.py
Static data loader: treasury-cashflow-simulation/src/load_static.py
Movement generator: treasury-cashflow-simulation/src/generate_movements.py
Sweep engine: treasury-cashflow-simulation/src/sweep_engine.py
Balances preparation: treasury-cashflow-simulation/src/balances_engine.py



Outputs

treasury-cashflow-simulation/data/Balances/balances_YYYYMMDD.csv
treasury-cashflow-simulation/data/Movements/movements_YYYYMMDD.csv
PostgreSQL tables: treasury_balances, treasury_movements



Code walkthrough
Explain key modules and functions used in the simulation. Use the code cells below to show examples and small excerpts.

# Example: show latest 5 movements from PostgreSQL (safe if DATABASE_URL is missing)
import os
import pandas as pd

try:
    from dotenv import load_dotenv
    from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text

    load_dotenv()
    database_url = os.getenv('DATABASE_URL')
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    database_url = None

if database_url:
    engine = create_engine(database_url)
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        df = pd.read_sql(text('SELECT * FROM treasury_movements ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 5'), conn)
        display(df)
else:
    print('DATABASE_URL not found. Showing a generated sample:')
    sample = pd.DataFrame({
        'date': ['2026-07-30','2026-07-30','2026-07-29'],

        'account_number': ['1001','1002','1001'],

    })
    display(sample)
